name: When should I repair a broken window versus replacing the entire window?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair a broken window versus replacing the entire window?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing a broken window glass is typically possible if only the glass pane is damaged and the window frame remains intact and functional. This is often more cost-effective. However, if the frame is warped, rotted, or significantly damaged, or if the window mechanism is failing, a full window replacement is usually recommended. Modern windows also offer better energy efficiency, so an older, inefficient window with broken glass might be better replaced entirely for long-term savings.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repairing just the glass is suitable if the frame is in good condition; replace the whole window if the frame or mechanism is damaged, or for energy efficiency upgrades.
